title: Correct a landed specification defect: the record carries both anchors the doctrine says it lacks -- two surfaces corrected, one digest-sealed export deliberately left
objective: Remove a false claim from main. The #278 doctrine tells a builder that closing the in-place severity-edit route needs 'the sealed input digest or an equivalent anchor' and that the edit is 'undetectable without a baseline the record does not carry'. Both anchors exist; the sentence sends the reader away from them.
business_value: A specification defect in doctrine costs whoever acts on it the whole design. This one names a mechanism to build that is already present, and mis-states which of two existing anchors is unavailable and why.
in_scope: docs/governance/GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md: correct the in-place-severity-edit declaration with the measured position, carrying the retracted text visibly; add the note recording that BADF-DEM-0113 is deliberately left uncorrected and why; record the re-test of the sibling ACCEPTED_BY_AUTHORITY declaration (it HOLDS) and the caution that its suggested remedy models on decision_ref, which is itself required-and-unread (#292)
work/WP-2026-0127/work-package.json: correct the same claim in out_of_scope[1]
work/WP-2026-0130/work-package.json: the inherited reconcile (landed 9fad369), derived output of `badf_gate.py reconcile`
out_of_scope: badf/demands/BADF-DEM-0113.json -- DELIBERATELY NOT CORRECTED. A digest-sealed provenance export of issue #271's body; its function is to record what was believed at export time, wrong or not. Correcting it would break source.body_digest and falsify the artifact that exists to preserve the original. Verified byte-identical to origin/main with the digest recomputing.
Closing any of #280's four weakening routes. All four need schema changes and a corroboration decision; this WP corrects the record and changes no behaviour. #280 stays open.
Making body_digest enforced. It is referenced 0 times in scripts/ -- another member of #292's required-and-unread class, recorded on #295 rather than filed as a fourth instance.
change_class_rationale: Documentation and declaration correction. No code, no schema, no behaviour change. Reversible by reverting one squash commit.
data_classification_rationale: Governance prose and public-repo issue text.
acceptance_criteria: No surface still ASSERTS 'a baseline the record does not carry' or 'the sealed input digest or an equivalent anchor'; the phrases survive only inside the corrections, quoted as retracted.
Verified by a SUBJECT-WIDE sweep with every hit classified, not by matching the original wording -- the rider named one surface and the sweep found three.
badf/demands/BADF-DEM-0113.json is byte-identical to origin/main and source.body_digest still recomputes over its stored problem text. Asserted, not assumed.
The doctrine records that the export is deliberately left, and why, so the next sweep does not 'fix' it.

Open-ended clause (#270): what ELSE did #278 assert that later measurement contradicts? The sibling ACCEPTED_BY_AUTHORITY declaration was re-tested and HOLDS (authority has exactly one property and one required field; no accepted_by/approver/principal anywhere) -- recorded, because a correction that fixes one claim and leaves its neighbour untested is the failure this repo keeps paying for.
evidence: subject-wide sweep with every hit classified
sibling declaration re-tested against the schema
evidence_obligations: the sweep is reported as 'N hits on pattern P, classified', never as the bare verb 'swept' -- the pattern is a hypothesis about phrasing
the untouched-export claim is verified by byte comparison against origin/main AND digest recomputation, not by intent
risk_factors: A correction that restores a digest-sealed export would silently rewrite history; the WP declares the export untouched and asserts the seal rather than relying on care.
A phrase-matched sweep would miss a re-worded assertion. The sweep is by subject; the residual is that phrasing is an open space and no sweep is exhaustive over the claim.

Bound as WP-2026-0132 / BADF-DEM-0118 before publishing a claim; both were already taken (SARCHI #294, BARCHI-3 #277). Rotated to 0133/0120 with the claim published first. The branch was unpushed, so the collision was invisible to every surface another seat could read -- which is the non-coverage the publish-before-bind step exists to cover.

rollback.method: revert the squash commit via PR

tdd_exception.reason: Documentation and declaration correction with no behaviour change and no test obligations; the evidence is a classified subject-wide sweep plus a byte-identity and digest assertion on the deliberately-untouched export.
